Abstract: W e disclose an concise synthesis of alkynylcyclopropane derivatives containing adjacent quaternary
carbon centers via a transition-metal free cascade enyne rearrangement and cyclopropanation process. This
methodology , started from a variety of allenylphosphine oxides and N-tosylhydrazones, features the advantage
of transition-metal-free, operational simplicity , wide substrate scope and good functional group tolerance.
Keywords: Cascade Enyne Rearrangement and Cyclopropanation; Alkynylcyclopropane; T ransition-Metal-Free;
Allenylphosphine Oxides; N-tosylhydrazones
Intr oduction
The eff icient stereoselective synthesis of alkynyl-
cyclopropane derivatives are of current interest since
they play unique roles in biochemical processes, or
display interesting pharmacological properties. Exam-
ples including callipeltoside A (cytotoxic activity
against NSCLC � N6 human bronchopulmonary non-
small-cell lung carcinoma and P388 cells),
[1]
GT -2331
(protean agonist),

ortho-alkynylbenzoate (ABz, novel leaving group of

Moreover , alkynyl cyclopropanes also constitute
useful substrates for numerous chemical
transformations

among which the functional conversion of alkynes is
considered to be the most effective strategy (Sche-

T o the best of our knowledge, allenes which act as

attention on the synthesis of alkynylcyclopropanes.
These limited reports are mainly focused on reactions
via alkynyl carbene

or intramolecular alkynyl
cyclopropanation

process. W e envisioned that a
reaction involving intermediate state of conjugated
enyne may provide novel protocol to construct alkynyl
cyclopropanes which has not been reported so far . This
propose inspired us to design a new type of allenes to
achieve this transformation. In this regime, recently ,
our group has advanced a series of studies on a kind of
allenylphosphine oxides that promoted versatile syn-
thetic transformations including intramolecular rear-
rangement and intermolecular cyclopropanation, re-
spectively (Scheme 1B).
[13a,b]
As part of our continuing
interest in allene and N-tosylhydrazone chemistry ,

based on the couplings of 1,1,3-trisubstituted allenyl-
phosphine oxides with N-tosylhydrazones (Sche-

Results and Discussion
T o rationalize our hypothesis, our discovery and initial
development of this reaction is summarized in T able 1.
The substrates of allenylphosphine oxide (1 a) and 2 a
were submitted to various conditions. The initial
attempt utilizing a mixture of 3 equiv . of K
2

alkynylcyclopropane 3 aa in 65% isolated yield and
4.9:1 dr (trans:cis) (entry 1). Subsequent screening of
bases and solvents revealed that K
2
CO
3
was the best in
terms of dr value (entries 1–6), and 1.4-dioxane was
the optimal solvent in terms of both reaction eff iciency
and dr value (entries 7–14). In view of our previous
work,
[13b]
we found that the addition of 20 mol% 1,10-
phen resulted in a great increase in product yield (91%
yield), albeit with a slightly diminished dr value after
some trials with various additives (entries 15–20).
Further evaluation of its loading (entries 21–23) led to
lower yield. Moreover , control experiment revealed
that the base was indispensable to obtain the product
(entry 24). Therefore we choose the condition in
entry 15 with the highest yield as the standard
condition, although the dr value is not the highest.
W ith the optimal conditions in hand, the scope of
the cascade enyne rearrangement and cyclo-propana-
tion reaction was investigated. Structural variations on
the alkynyl unit of the allenylphosphine oxides were
examined (Scheme 2 A). All reactions smoothly took
place under standard conditions to furnish alkynylcy-
clopropane 3 aa–3 ka in good yields (57–91%). The
relative stereochemistry of trans-isomer was assigned
based on the X-ray crystallographic analysis of 3 ba
(CCDC: 2034008).
[14]
Furthermore, the position of the
substituents (para, meta, or ortho) was found to have
little impact on the eff iciency of this transformation
(3 ca, 3 ga, and 3 ha). As for the stereoselectivity , all of
the substrates tested, with either electron-donating (4-

the product trans-3 aa, which rationalized the trans-

[15]
Conclusion
In summary , we have reported a transition-metal-free
cascade enyne rearrangement and cyclopropanation
reaction between N-tosylhydrazones and allenylphos-
phine oxides. This protocol provides a straight way to
aff ord the various adjacent quaternary carbon centers
containing alkynylcyclopropane derivatives in high
yields via a [3 + 2] cycloaddition process. The key step
of the reaction depends on the formation of the
intermediate conjugated enyne. Further investigations
towards the synthetic applications of the alkynyl
cyclopropanes are ongoing in our laboratory .
